title: Finite type points meet every nonempty locally closed subset of any scheme
statement: Let $V$ be any scheme [def-pc-scheme]. A point $v\in V$ is called a finite type point if the canonical morphism $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(v)\to V$ is of finite type [def-weil-residue-field, def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Let $Z\subseteq|V|$ be a nonempty locally closed subset, meaning an intersection of an open subset and a closed subset. Then $Z$ contains a finite type point of $V$. Consequently every open subset $O\subseteq|V|$ containing every finite type point equals $|V|$. No Jacobson, Noetherian, quasi-compactness, or separatedness hypothesis is imposed on $V$.

source.place: Tag 02J4 (lemma-enough-finite-type-points); finite type point as in Tag 02J1 (definition-finite-type-point).

proof.text: Write $Z=G\cap C$, where $G\subseteq V$ is open and $C\subseteq V$ is closed, and choose $z_0\in Z$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis] to $z_0\in G$ to obtain an affine open $W$ of $V$ with $z_0\in W\subseteq G$. In the open subscheme $W$, the subset $D=C\cap W=Z\cap W$ is closed and nonempty (it contains $z_0$).

source.place: Tag 01IT (lemma-basis-affine-opens); affine-local version of Tag 02J4, proof

proof.text: The affine scheme $W$ is quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs]. It is Kolmogorov: by [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-sober], every irreducible closed subset has a unique generic point. The closure of a point is irreducible: an open meeting its closure must contain the point, since otherwise its closed complement would contain the closure; hence two such opens meet at the point. If two points had the same closure, both would be generic points of that irreducible closed subset and hence equal; thus distinct points have different closures, equivalently some open set contains exactly one of them. Apply [lem-sc-quasi-compact-kolmogorov-closed-point] to the nonempty closed subset $D$ of $W$. It gives $v\in D$ with $\{v\}$ closed in $W$. In particular $v\in Z$.

source.place: Tag 005E (lemma-quasi-compact-closed-point), applied to a closed subset; Schemes Tag 01IS (lemma-scheme-sober); Algebra Tag 00E8 (lemma-quasi-compact)

proof.text: The inclusion $j:W\to V$ is an open immersion as in [def-weil-open-immersion]. Identify $\mathcal O_{V,v}$ with $\mathcal O_{W,v}$ using [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk]: send the germ of $s\in\mathcal O_V(A)$ to the germ of $s|_{A\cap W}$. Conversely, an open neighbourhood of $v$ in $W$ is open in $V$ and has the same sections of the restricted structure sheaf, so send its germ to the same germ in $V$. The stated germ-equality criterion makes these maps well-defined; restriction preserves ring operations, and the two composites fix every germ. This ring isomorphism identifies the unique maximal ideals and hence the residue quotients $\kappa_V(v)$ and $\kappa_W(v)$ [def-weil-residue-field]. Composing $i_v:\operatorname{Spec}\kappa_W(v)\to W$ with $j$ gives the canonical residue-field morphism to $V$: its map on each neighbourhood is the germ map followed by the residue quotient, exactly the defining map for $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa_V(v)\to V$.

source.place: Tag 02J2 (lemma-identify-finite-type-points), identification under open restriction; Schemes Tag 01J9 (lemma-characterize-points)

proof.text: Since $\{v\}$ is closed in $W$, [lem-trf-closed-point-residue-immersion] makes $i_v$ a closed immersion. Its composite with the open immersion $j$ is an immersion by the factorization definition in [def-weil-closed-immersion]. By clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-immersion-base-change-lft], this composite, hence the canonical morphism $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa_V(v)\to V$ from step 3, is locally of finite type.

source.place: Tag 01T5 (lemma-immersion-locally-finite-type), second assertion; Tag 02J2 (lemma-identify-finite-type-points), closed-point implication

proof.text: The space $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa_V(v)$ has a single point [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. For every affine open of $V$, its inverse image under this morphism is either empty or that singleton and is therefore quasi-compact: the empty space has the empty subcover, and an open cover of a singleton has a one-element subcover. Thus the morphism is quasi-compact, and together with step 4 it is of finite type by [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. This proves that $v\in Z$ is a finite type point of $V$.

source.place: Tag 01TA (lemma-point-finite-type), proof of (1) equivalent to (2); Tag 02J4 (lemma-enough-finite-type-points)

proof.text: Let $O\subseteq|V|$ be open and contain every finite type point. If $O\ne|V|$, its complement $C=|V|\setminus O$ is a nonempty closed subset, hence a locally closed subset (intersect it with the open $|V|$). Applying steps 1--5 with $Z=C$ gives a finite type point in $C$, contradicting the hypothesis on $O$. Therefore $O=|V|$. When $V$ is empty the equality holds immediately.

source.place: Tag 02J4 (lemma-enough-finite-type-points), consequence for complements of opens

proof_origin.place: Tag 02J4 (lemma-enough-finite-type-points), affine-local elaboration using Tags 02J2, 01TA and 01T5; closed point chosen in a closed subset of an affine neighbourhood rather than after constructing a reduced subscheme.
